newsitem.title: USA: Scholastic sees improved earnings next year.
newsitem.headline: Scholastic sees improved earnings next year.

text.p: Scholastic Corp said Thursday it expects about break-even results in the fiscal year ending May 31.

The company said it expects significantly improved earnings and positive cash flow in the new fiscal year starting June 1, as it cuts annual costs by at least $25 million, in part by eliminating more than 400 jobs, and refocuses on its core businesses to improve profitability.
The company said job cuts include an approximate 10 percent staff reduction in New York.
The company also said it would cut costs by closing its operations in France.

The company said it has retained the investment banking firm of Veronis & Suhler to sell two of its consumer magazines, Home Computing and Small Business Computing. The company said the two profitable magazines - for adults - did not fit their strategic focus.
The company also said it would close magazines "such as Agenda, Superscience, Red and Math Power." No further information was immediately available on magazine closings.
Scholastic said it would sublease more 40,000 square feet of New York office space.
The company said it will replace a portion of cash compensation for executives with stock options.
The company also said it will consolidate four instructional divisions into one school group and improve its purchasing terms with suppliers.

The company said its current results are due to lower than expected fourth quarter revenues, further increases in reserves for trade book returns and inventory, and additional restructuring charges related to new cost-reduction actions.
